description: احب البرمجه وصانع برنامج يعرفك الاساسيات وندربك علي بناء برامج تحاكي الفضاء
summary: Mr. Zero is an interactive, browser-based Python 3.12 learning laboratory powered by WebAssembly (Pyodide) and 10+ official NASA APIs. Designed for Arabic-speaking beginners, it turns live spacecraft, planetary, and Earth-observation data into visual, executable code. Students write Python in a live editor with a Memory Board showing every variable's type and value, an Arabic error explainer for tracebacks, and a rule-based PEP 8 reviewer requiring zero external LLM API keys. Seven progressive lessons and five live quizzes pull real telemetry—including ISS orbital vectors (JPL Horizons), Mars Curiosity REMS weather, Perseverance rover photos, near-Earth asteroids (JPL SBDB & NeoWs), DSCOVR EPIC Earth imagery, and NASA Exoplanet Archive records. Selecting any of 29 celestial models, asteroids, or exoplanets loads its complete NASA physical dossier, photo gallery, and runnable Python script on an interactive hologram canvas.
details:
What it does:

Mr. Zero is a full-stack interactive Python 3.12 learning platform in Arabic backed entirely by live official NASA APIs. It features seven progressive telemetry-driven lessons (variables, conditionals, loops, lists, custom functions, time-series analysis, and None data cleaning), an editor with line numbers, in-browser Python execution via Pyodide WebAssembly, a live Memory Visualizer, an Arabic traceback explainer, a deterministic PEP 8 reviewer (0–100 score), Zero Pro study tools (focus timer, snapshots, daily NASA challenge, 5 live quizzes, completion certificate), and a programmable 3D-style SVG Hologram Stage with 29 NASA mission/celestial models. Selecting any model, asteroid, or exoplanet opens a full NASA dossier containing live JPL Horizons vectors, orbital elements, Mars Curiosity REMS 7-sol weather, Perseverance raw photos, an 8-photo official NASA gallery, and one-click Python code injection.

Tools and technologies:

Frontend: React 19, TypeScript, Vite 8, Tailwind CSS v4, Lucide Icons, and Google Fonts (Tajawal & JetBrains Mono).

In-Browser Runtime: Pyodide 0.26.4 (CPython 3.12 compiled to WebAssembly) served from same-origin Express routes with ZIP header pre-verification.

Backend: Node.js 22 & Express server aggregating and caching 10+ official NASA APIs without exposing keys to the browser.

Creativity and impact:

Most beginner coding tools only print pass/fail using synthetic numbers. Mr. Zero exposes what Python is doing in memory step by step, explains errors in Arabic, and connects every Python concept directly to real-time NASA telemetry—bridging open space science and Arabic STEM education with zero setup required by students.

Known limitations:

Python runs on the main browser thread, so heavy infinite loops can briefly pause UI responsiveness. The editor detects and blocks unguarded while True loops without break before execution, and moving Pyodide execution into an isolated Web Worker is the next planned milestone.
